kind.text: I am steady. I am allowed to take up space, and I trust the pace I am moving at today. I do not need to be finished to be worthy of rest. When something is hard, I can slow down, ask for help, and speak to myself as I would to a friend.
You can be patient with yourself the way you are patient with a friend who is learning. You are allowed to go slowly. You are allowed to begin again, and the beginning still counts.
Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for a kindness.
kind.author: Seneca

kind.text: I do not have to earn rest by finishing everything first. Rest is part of the work, not a reward for it. I can stop when I am tired and start again when I am ready.
My worth is not measured by how much I get done today. A slow day is still a day I lived well. I will do what I can and let that be a full account.
Find fault with nobody. If you can, set the doer right; if that is impossible, at least set the thing right; if even that cannot be, to what purpose is your fault-finding?
kind.author: Marcus Aurelius

kind.text: I speak to myself all day long. Today I will use the tone I would use with someone I care about. If I would not say it to a friend, I do not need to say it to myself.
Making a mistake means I tried something. I can name what went wrong without deciding what it says about me. Then I fix what I can and move on to the next thing.

Do not be ashamed of being helped. It is incumbent upon you to do your appointed work, like a soldier in the breach. What if you are lame and cannot scale the battlement alone, but can with another's help?
kind.author: Marcus Aurelius

kind.text: Patience with others begins with patience for myself. When I am gentle with my own slow progress, I have more gentleness left over for everyone else.
Everyone I meet today is carrying something I cannot see. I do not need to know what it is to be kind. A little warmth costs me nothing and may be the best part of someone's day.
Kindness is invincible if only it is honest, not fawning or insincere.
kind.author: Marcus Aurelius

kind.text: Being tired is information, not a verdict on my effort. When I am worn out, the kind response is rest, not a lecture. I can give myself what I would gladly give anyone else.
I am allowed to go slowly. Starting again is not failing; it is how anything gets learned. Each new beginning counts as much as the first one did.
When, therefore, anyone provokes you, be assured that it is your own opinion which provokes you. Try, therefore, in the first place, not to be hurried away with the appearance.
kind.author: Epictetus

kind.text: I can be kind and still be honest. Kindness is not saying yes to everything. It is telling the truth in a way that leaves the other person standing.
I do not have to fix everyone's problems to be a good friend. Sometimes the kindest thing is to listen until they finish. My attention is a gift, and it is enough.
If then you wish not to be of an angry temper, do not feed the habit; throw nothing on it which will increase it: at first keep quiet, and count the days on which you have not been angry.
kind.author: Epictetus

kind.text: Nobody is grading my day. I can leave a task unfinished and still deserve to sit down. Tonight I will stop at a reasonable hour and let tomorrow have what is left.
When I want to snap at someone, I can pause first. One breath gives me a choice about what I say next. I will lower my voice and say one honest sentence.
It helps little to have cast out your own faults if you must quarrel with those of others.
kind.author: Seneca

kind.text: Asking for help is not a weakness. It is how work gets done and how people grow closer. Today I can ask for what I need in plain words.
Comparing myself to others takes attention away from my own path. Their progress takes nothing from mine. I can be glad for them and keep going at my own pace.
Call to mind what honourable or brave deeds you have done; consider the good side of your own life.
kind.author: Seneca

kind.text: I can forgive myself for what I did not know before I learned it. Hindsight is not fair to the person I was. I will use what I know now and let the rest go.
Someone else's bad mood does not have to become mine. I can notice it, stay steady, and respond with care instead of matching it. Their storm is theirs to weather.
There remains much more of the road than we have put behind us; but the greater part of progress is the desire to progress.
kind.author: Seneca

kind.text: Doing less than I planned is not the same as failing. Plans are guesses about the future, and the future is often busier than expected. I will adjust the plan instead of blaming myself.
Small kindnesses add up. A thank-you, a held door, a short message: none of them take long. Today I will do one small kind thing without waiting for a reason.
We must humour our minds and grant them rest from time to time, which acts upon them like food, and restores their strength.
kind.author: Seneca

kind.text: I do not have to be productive to be worthy of care. My value was never in my output. When I rest, I am not wasting time; I am looking after the person who does the work.
If someone is unkind to me, I can choose not to pass it on. I can state my point once, calmly, and leave the rest. Answering anger with steadiness is a strength.

However mean your life is, meet it and live it; do not shun it and call it hard names. It is not so bad as you are. It looks poorest when you are richest. The fault-finder will find faults even in paradise. Love your life, poor as it is.
kind.author: Henry David Thoreau

kind.text: Slowing down is allowed. Hurry is a habit, not a requirement, and most of what I rush would be better done at a steadier pace. Today I will finish one thing before starting the next.
Taking care of my body is not vanity or indulgence. Food, water, sleep, and movement are basic maintenance. I will give myself the care I would insist on for anyone I love.
Be not hasty, neither speak too loud, nor be too urgent, and so what you desire will be sooner and better accomplished.
kind.author: Plutarch

kind.text: I can hold high standards and still treat myself gently when I miss them. A standard is a direction, not a judge. I will note the gap, learn from it, and try again tomorrow.
Criticism can be useful without being a verdict. I can take the part that is true and set down the rest. What I keep, I will act on. What I do not keep, I let pass.
Praise from others must come unasked: we must concern ourselves with the healing of our own lives.
kind.author: Epicurus

kind.text: Saying no is a form of kindness too. Every yes I cannot afford costs someone later, usually me. I can decline clearly and without a long apology.
I am not behind. There is no schedule I was supposed to keep except the one I made up. I can set a fair pace for today and trust it.
Guilt about what I cannot do steals time from what I can do. I will do the one thing within my reach today and let that be my contribution.
Gentleness is not weakness. It takes strength to stay calm when I am frustrated. When I feel myself hardening, I will breathe and choose the gentler response.
Not every thought about myself is true. The thought that I am not enough is a thought, not a fact. I can notice it, name it, and go back to what I was doing.
Rest is not a reward for finishing. It is what makes finishing possible. I can rest before I am exhausted, and I do not need anyone's permission.
Being unwell is not a failure of willpower. Slowing down to recover is the treatment, not an indulgence. I will cancel what can be cancelled and let my body do its work.
When someone is late, or forgets, or falls short, I can assume the ordinary explanation. Most people are doing their best with what they have. I will offer the patience I hope to receive.
I can give someone my full attention for the length of one conversation. No planning my reply, no glancing away. Being heard is one of the kindest things I can offer.
I do not have to be good at something to be allowed to enjoy it. Beginners deserve encouragement, and I am allowed to be one. I will practice today without keeping score.

pres.text: Right now there is a breath moving in and out. I can feel my feet on the floor and the weight of my hands. Nothing in this moment needs solving. I only need to be here for it.
I can only do one thing at a time. When my mind runs ahead to the next task, I bring it back to the one in my hands. This one is the only one I can actually do.
Lay hold of to-day's task, and you will not need to depend so much upon to-morrow's. While we are postponing, life speeds by.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: Worry about the future does not change the future. It only spends the present. I will bring my attention back to what is in front of me and do that one thing well.
I do not have to feel calm to act well. I can be unsettled and still do the next small thing. Steadiness usually follows action, not the other way around.
All difficult things in the world are sure to arise from a previous state in which they were easy, and all great things from one in which they were small.
pres.author: Laozi

pres.text: When everything feels like too much, I am usually carrying the whole day at once. I can set the day down. The next ten minutes are all I have to manage, and I can manage ten minutes.
Before I start anything, I will take three slow breaths. Then I will begin. The task does not need me to arrive at it in a hurry.
Let us spend one day as deliberately as Nature, and not be thrown off the track by every nutshell and mosquito's wing that falls on the rails.
pres.author: Henry David Thoreau
pres.work: Walden, Where I Lived, and What I Lived For

pres.text: Listening is a form of presence. When someone speaks, I can hear them out instead of preparing my answer. I will decide what to say when they have finished.
A tight chest and fast thoughts are a body under strain, not a verdict on my life. I can unclench my jaw, drop my shoulders, and return to the task that is already open.
Practise attention to what others say, and do your best to get into the speaker's mind.
pres.author: Marcus Aurelius

pres.text: Thoughts about the past are only thoughts. The event is over. I can notice a replay, name it, and turn my attention back to what is happening now.
The present moment is the only place I can act. The past is finished and the future has not arrived. Whatever I do next happens here, so here is where I will put my attention.
Stick only to the work in hand, and to the tool you have for doing it.
pres.author: Marcus Aurelius

pres.text: Ordinary things are not waiting to become something else. A warm cup, a quiet room, a cool morning. I can meet each one as it is and let that be the whole task.
I can turn off the noise for an hour. Nothing that arrives in that hour will matter more than the thing I am doing. When the hour ends, I will look at what came in, all at once.
Always keep strictly to the first impressions, without adding comments of your own, and you are unaffected.
pres.author: Marcus Aurelius

pres.text: Trouble asks a simple question: what can I do about this right now? If there is something, I do it. If there is nothing, I return to my breath and my work.
Waiting is only wasted time if I spend it wishing it were over. I can use the minutes as they are: to breathe, to look around, to let my mind rest.
If it is good to use attention to-morrow, how much better is it to do so to-day?
pres.author: Epictetus

pres.text: My attention is the most valuable thing I have. I do not need to give it to everything that asks. Today I will choose where it goes and keep it there.
When I eat, I can just eat. When I walk, I can just walk. Doing one thing fully is more restful than doing three things halfway.

Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions: the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running. If you would be a good reader, read; if a writer, write.
pres.author: Epictetus

pres.text: Impatience is a signal that I have left the present for a future I cannot reach yet. I can notice it, come back, and let the moment take the time it takes.
I notice the urge to check, to refresh, to look again. Checking is not the same as knowing. I can let the urge pass and return to what I was doing.
Even bad fortune is fickle. Perhaps it will come, perhaps not; in the meantime it is not. So look forward to better things.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: Slowing down does not mean falling behind. It means being where I am. Work done with full attention is usually done faster and better than work done in a rush.
I do not have to make today good. I only have to meet it. A decent day is enough: some food, some movement, a little quiet, and no big decisions when I am tired.
It is indeed foolish to be unhappy now because you may be unhappy at some future time.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: Anger rises fast and passes if I let it. I do not need to reply this second. I can feel the heat, notice the story forming, and give it a full minute before I act.
Rest is a form of presence too. I can sit still without earning it, without distraction, without a plan. Doing nothing for a few minutes is not a waste of time.
Past and future are both absent; we feel neither of them. But there can be no pain except as the result of what you feel.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: Sleep does not come to a busy mind. I can put the day away, turn off the light, and lie still. Lying quietly in the dark is enough of a plan.
Between finishing one thing and starting the next there is a pause. I can take it. A moment of stillness before the next task is where I catch up with myself.
Hence, every day ought to be regulated as if it closed the series, as if it rounded out and completed our existence.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: A hard moment is one moment. It does not have to become the whole day. I can let it be what it is, breathe through it, and notice when it passes.
Being present with someone means putting down what I am doing before I greet them. Hands empty, eyes up. It costs a few seconds and changes the whole conversation.
Whenever a controversy seems likely to be longer or more keenly disputed than usual, let us check its first beginnings, before it gathers strength.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: When my mind says hurry, I can check whether anything actually requires it. Most of the time nothing does. I can move at the pace of the task, not the pace of my worry.
The body is always in the present. When my thoughts race ahead, I can return to it: feet on the floor, breath moving, weight in the chair. It is a place I can always come back to.
People do not all take offence in the same way; you ought then to know what your own weak point is, that you may guard it with especial care.
pres.author: Seneca

pres.text: I do not need an opinion about everything that happens today. I can notice, let it pass, and save my attention for what matters. Most things do not need my comment.
Attention is a skill. It grows by being used, like any other. Each time I bring my mind back to the present, I am getting better at bringing it back.
The future is not to be waited for; the past is not to be sought again!
pres.author: Zhuangzi

pres.text: Nothing I am doing right now is a rehearsal for something else. This meal, this walk, this conversation is the real thing. I will give it the attention that real things deserve.
I can pause before I answer. A short silence is not awkward; it is thinking. I will let the question land, take a breath, and then say what I actually mean.
There were times when I could not afford to sacrifice the bloom of the present moment to any work, whether of the head or hands.
pres.author: Henry David Thoreau

pres.text: To finish the moment, to find the journey's end in every step of the road, to live the greatest number of good hours, is wisdom.
pres.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

persp.text: Most of what worries me today will not matter in a year. I can hold my plans loosely and let the day change them. What is mine to do, I will do. What is not mine, I can set down.
I do not have to force today into the shape I planned. When something will not bend, I can bend instead. I will do the task in front of me, stop when it is done, and let that be enough.
Some things are in our control and others not. Things in our control are opinion, pursuit, desire, aversion, and, in a word, whatever are our own actions.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: Some things are up to me: my effort, my attention, my words. Most other things are not. I will put my energy where it can make a difference and let the rest go.
A mistake is information about one thing, not a verdict on the whole day. Name what went wrong in one plain sentence. Fix what can be fixed. Then give the next task your full attention.
Don't demand that things happen as you wish, but wish that they happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: Too much is usually many things stacked into one feeling. Write them down. Cross off what is not due today. Cross off what belongs to someone else. What remains is a list, not a weight.
At the end of the day I ask two questions. What did I actually do, and what did I only worry about? The second list is usually longer. Tomorrow I will move one item from it to the first.
How often has the unexpected happened! How often has the expected never come to pass! And even though it is ordained to be, what does it avail to run out to meet your suffering?
persp.author: Seneca

persp.text: Waiting for a reply, a result, or a decision, I keep rehearsing every outcome. None of the rehearsals change the result. I will do the step that is the same in every case and let the rest wait.
Not every problem needs solving today. Some will look smaller in the morning. Some will solve themselves. I will decide what is truly urgent and leave the rest for tomorrow.
It is better to leave a vessel unfilled, than to attempt to carry it when it is full.
persp.author: Laozi

persp.text: No news is not bad news. It is only no news. I will stop writing other people's reasons for them and give the answer time to arrive.
Other people's choices are theirs. I can offer help, state my view once, and then let them decide. My job is what I do, not what they do with it.
As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
persp.author: The Buddha

persp.text: When a plan falls through, I can give myself a few minutes to be annoyed. Then I ask what is possible now. There is usually a smaller, useful thing waiting. I start on that.
Being productive is not the point of being alive. Some days the most useful thing I can do is rest, think, or spend time with someone. Those days count too.
Do not live as though you had a thousand years before you. The common due impends; while you live, and while you may, be good.
persp.author: Marcus Aurelius

persp.text: Wanting more is a habit that never finishes on its own. Enough is a real amount, and I can name it. Anything beyond it is a choice, not a need.
Praise and blame both pass. Neither one changes the quality of what I did. I can take the useful part of each and let the rest go.
Most of the things we say or do are not necessary; get rid of them, and you will gain time and tranquillity.
persp.author: Marcus Aurelius

persp.text: Bad news lands harder when I am tired and hungry. Before I decide what it means, I will eat, drink some water, and take a short walk. Then I will look again and choose one next step.
Nothing is gained by hurrying through a hard problem. Speed adds mistakes. I will slow down, do one part well, and let the rest follow in order.
The gourd is bitter: drop it then! There are brambles in the path: then turn aside! It is enough. Do not go on to argue, Why pray have these things a place in the world?
persp.author: Marcus Aurelius

persp.text: I cannot control the outcome, only the attempt. I will make the attempt as well as I can and then let the result be what it is. That is the whole of my job.
Half of most criticism is fair and half is not. I can take the fair half without signing for the rest. I will write down the one true point and act on it.
If it is not your duty, do not do it: if it is not true, do not say it.
persp.author: Marcus Aurelius

persp.text: Someone else's anger is mostly about them. I do not have to catch every word. I can listen for the part I can fix and let the rest pass.
Winning an argument often costs more than it is worth. I can keep the relationship and lose the point. I will ask what the other person is worried about before I give my view.
Sickness is a hindrance to the body, but not to your ability to choose, unless that is your choice. Lameness is a hindrance to the leg, but not to your ability to choose.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: What I own is enough for today. The next thing will look essential until I have it, and then it will sit in a drawer. Before I buy anything, I will wait two nights and see if I still want it.
Dread makes me pay for a hard thing twice: once in worry and once in fact. I will face the hard thing this morning and free the rest of the day.
Be assured, then, that when your own cup likewise is broken, you ought to be affected just as when another's cup was broken. Apply this in like manner to greater things.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: Comparison changes nothing about my life except how I feel about it. What others have takes nothing from me. I can be glad for them and return to my own work.
Things will be messy again tomorrow. That is not failure; it is how life works. I will do what is needed tonight and leave the rest for the morning.

Is anything brought around to you? Put out your hand and take your share with moderation. Does it pass by you? Don't stop it. Is it not yet come? Don't stretch your desire towards it, but wait till it reaches you.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: Delays happen on their own schedule, not mine. I can spend the wait annoyed or spend it on something I chose. The wait is the same length either way.
Most of what I say and do is not necessary. If I drop what does not matter, I gain time and quiet. Today I will ask of each task: does this need doing at all?

In every affair consider what precedes and follows, and then undertake it. Otherwise you will begin with spirit; but not having thought of the consequences, when some of them appear you will shamefully desist.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: Saying yes to everything means saying no to what matters most. I will decline one thing today that does not need me and say so in a single sentence.
I do not need to fix what is not mine to fix. I can offer support and then step back. Letting people handle their own lives is a form of respect.
Do you ask what is the proper limit to wealth? It is, first, to have what is necessary, and, second, to have what is enough.
persp.author: Seneca

persp.text: A hard day is still only one day. Tomorrow starts fresh whether today went well or not. I will finish what I can, sleep, and begin again.
Fewer things done with care beat many things done in a hurry. I will choose the one thing that matters most today and give it my full effort.

Recall your steps, therefore, from idle things, and when you would know whether that which you seek is based upon a natural or upon a misleading desire, consider whether it can stop at any definite point.
persp.author: Seneca

persp.text: I am not required to have the answer right away. Time makes most things clearer. When I am unsure and the decision allows it, I will wait a day before choosing.
Feelings are real, but they are not always accurate. Fear can overstate danger and disappointment can overstate loss. I will let a feeling settle before I act on it.
This is what happens when you hurry through a maze; the faster you go, the worse you are entangled.
persp.author: Seneca

persp.text: Success and failure are both temporary. Neither one is the end of the story. I can do good work today without needing today to decide everything.
The plan is a tool, not a promise. When the day changes, the plan can change with it. I will keep the goal and stay flexible about the route.
All things were ready for us at our birth; it is we that have made everything difficult for ourselves, through our disdain for what is easy.
persp.author: Seneca

persp.text: If you want to find out the truth about anything, commit the task to time: nothing can be accurately discerned at a time of disturbance.
persp.author: Seneca

persp.text: A pheasant of the marshes has to take ten steps to pick up a mouthful of food, and thirty steps to get a drink, but it does not seek to be nourished in a coop.
persp.author: Zhuangzi

persp.text: But while you cannot regulate yourself, what leisure have you to be regulating the world?
persp.author: Zhuangzi

persp.text: Shall we always study to obtain more of these things, and not sometimes to be content with less?
persp.author: Henry David Thoreau

persp.text: Do not trouble yourself much to get new things, whether clothes or friends. Turn the old; return to them. Things do not change; we change.
persp.author: Henry David Thoreau

persp.text: Regret calamities, if you can thereby help the sufferer; if not, attend your own work, and already the evil begins to be repaired.
persp.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

persp.text: What I must do is all that concerns me, not what the people think.
persp.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

persp.text: So true is it that nothing is wretched, but thinking makes it so, and conversely every lot is happy if borne with equanimity.
persp.author: Boethius

persp.text: Some fear overmuch what they have strength to bear; others despise overmuch that to which their strength is unequal.
persp.author: Boethius

persp.text: We should not spoil what we have by desiring what we have not, but remember that what we have too was the gift of fortune.
persp.author: Epicurus

persp.text: We must heal our misfortunes by the grateful recollection of what has been and by the recognition that it is impossible to make undone what has been done.
persp.author: Epicurus
